claim: Rab5 translocates from early endosomes to mitochondria upon oxidative stress.
source: Here, by investigating mitochondrial-endosomal contact sites we made the surprising observation that the small GTPase Rab5 translocates from early endosomes to mitochondria upon oxidative stress.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in multiple figures throughout the manuscript.

claim: The translocation of Rab5 to mitochondria is reversible.
source: This process is reversible and accompanied by an increase in Rab5-positive endosomes in contact with mitochondria.
evidence: The abstract states this explicitly, and Figure 8 provides experimental data showing reversibility.

claim: Activation of Rab5 on mitochondria depends on the Rab5-GEF ALS2/Alsin.
source: Interestingly, activation of Rab5 on mitochondria depends on the Rab5-GEF ALS2/Alsin, encoded by a gene mutated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, supported by experimental data in Figures 10 and 11.

claim: Alsin-deficient human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived spinal motor neurons are defective in relocating Rab5 to mitochondria.
source: Alsin-deficient human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived spinal motor neurons are defective in relocating Rab5 to mitochondria and display increased susceptibility to oxidative stress.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, supported by experimental data in Figure 11.

claim: Alsin-deficient iPSC-derived spinal motor neurons display increased susceptibility to oxidative stress.
source: Alsin-deficient human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived spinal motor neurons are defective in relocating Rab5 to mitochondria and display increased susceptibility to oxidative stress.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, supported by experimental data in Figure 11D showing increased cytochrome c release.

claim: Membrane contact sites between ER and mitochondria are important for Ca2+ and lipid transfer.
source: For example, membrane contact sites (MCS) between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria are important for Ca2+ and lipid transfer (de Brito and Scorrano, 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Membrane contact sites between ER and mitochondria are important for mitochondria fission.
source: For example, membrane contact sites (MCS) between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria are important for Ca2+ and lipid transfer (de Brito and Scorrano, 2008), mitochondria fission (Friedman et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Membrane contact sites between ER and mitochondria are important for regulation of apoptosis.
source: For example, membrane contact sites (MCS) between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mitochondria are important for Ca2+ and lipid transfer (de Brito and Scorrano, 2008), mitochondria fission (Friedman et al., 2011), and regulation of apoptosis (Prudent et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Lipid droplets and peroxisomes interact with mitochondria to regulate fatty acid oxidation.
source: Lipid droplets and peroxisomes interact with mitochondria to regulate fatty acid oxidation (Cohen et al., 2014; Pu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Oxidized and damaged proteins can be selectively delivered to peroxisomes and lysosomes via mitochondrial-derived vesicles.
source: Oxidized and damaged proteins can be selectively delivered to peroxisomes and lysosomes via mitochondrial-derived vesicles (Sugiura et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Rab GTPases serve as molecular signatures on endosomes, regulating their biogenesis and functions.
source: Rab GTPases serve as molecular signatures on endosomes, regulating their biogenesis and functions (Pfeffer, 2017; Zerial and McBride, 2001; Zhen and Stenmark, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Ligand-receptor complexes at the plasma membrane are internalized into early endosomes marked by small GTPase Rab5.
source: Ligand-receptor complexes at the plasma membrane (PM) are internalized into early endosomes (EE) marked by small GTPase Rab5
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of endocytosis.

claim: Early endosomes can be recycled to the plasma membrane via Rab4 and Rab11-positive recycling endosomes.
source: Ligand-receptor complexes at the plasma membrane (PM) are internalized into early endosomes (EE) marked by small GTPase Rab5, followed by either recycling to the PM via Rab4 and Rab11-positive recycling endosomes (RE)
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of endocytosis.

claim: Early endosomes can be routed to late endosomes and lysosomes for degradation.
source: Ligand-receptor complexes at the plasma membrane (PM) are internalized into early endosomes (EE) marked by small GTPase Rab5, followed by either recycling to the PM via Rab4 and Rab11-positive recycling endosomes (RE), or routed to late endosomes (LE) and lysosomes for degradation.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of endocytosis.

claim: The conversion of Rab5-positive early endosomes into Rab7-positive late endosomes occurs during endosomal maturation.
source: The latter process occurs via the conversion of Rab5-positive EE into Rab7-positive LE (de Renzis et al., 2002; Rink et al., 2005; Sönnichsen et al., 2000; Ullrich et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: EEA1 is a dimeric coiled-coiled Rab5 effector protein that tethers two vesicles to allow efficient fusion between Rab5-harbouring membranes.
source: For example, EEA1 is a dimeric coiled-coiled Rab5 effector protein that tethers two vesicles to allow efficient fusion between Rab5-harbouring membranes (Murray et al., 2016; Ohya et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab5 effector APPL1 is involved in regulating metabolic and inflammatory responses.
source: Other Rab5 effectors such as APPL1 are involved in regulating metabolic and inflammatory responses (Schenck et al., 2008; Wen et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab activation on the membrane requires guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs).
source: Rab activation, and thus stabilization after recruitment, on the membrane requires guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs) (Blümer et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Rab5 GEFs constitute a family of VPS9 domain-containing proteins, including Rabex-5, RME-6, ALS2/Alsin, and Rin1-3.
source: Rab5 GEFs constitute a family of VPS9 domain-containing proteins, including Rabex-5 (Horiuchi et al., 1997), RME-6 (Sato et al., 2005), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis protein 2 (ALS2/Alsin) (Otomo et al., 2003), and mammalian Ras and Rab interactor 1, 2, 3 (Rin1-3) (Hu et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Transfer of iron from endosomes to mitochondria is mediated by physical interactions between the two organelles.
source: For example, transfer of iron (Das et al., 2016; Sheftel et al., 2007) and cholesterol (Charman et al., 2010) from endosomes to mitochondria is mediated by physical interactions between the two organelles.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Transfer of cholesterol from endosomes to mitochondria is mediated by physical interactions between the two organelles.
source: For example, transfer of iron (Das et al., 2016; Sheftel et al., 2007) and cholesterol (Charman et al., 2010) from endosomes to mitochondria is mediated by physical interactions between the two organelles.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Expression of pro-apoptotic factors such as canonical BH3-only proteins drive Rab5- and Rab7-positive endolysosomes into inner mitochondrial compartments via a pathway that appears to differ from autophagy/mitophagy.
source: Intriguingly, the expression of pro-apoptotic factors such as canonical BH3-only proteins drive Rab5- and Rab7-positive endolysosomes into inner mitochondrial compartments via a pathway that appears to differ from autophagy/mitophagy (Hamacher-Brady et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Approximately 8% of hit genes from a genome-wide RNAi screen of endocytosis had mitochondrial-related functions.
source: Interestingly, our previous conducted genome-wide RNAi screen of endocytosis (Collinet et al., 2010) revealed that ~8% of the hit genes had mitochondrial-related functions
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and represents data from that study.

claim: A subset of endosomes appear to partially overlap with, or are in close proximity to, mitochondria in HeLa cells.
source: We observed a subset of endosomes that appeared to partially overlap with, or were in close proximity to, mitochondria (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This observation is directly stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Transferrin-containing endosomes exhibit higher colocalization with mitochondria compared to EGF-containing structures at both 10 and 60 min time points.
source: In both time points, Tfn-containing endosomes consistently exhibited higher colocalization with Mito-Red (Figure 1D) compared to EGF-structures
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by quantitative colocalization analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Interactions with mitochondria may preferentially involve early/recycling endosomal structures.
source: In both time points, Tfn-containing endosomes consistently exhibited higher colocalization with Mito-Red (Figure 1D) compared to EGF-structures, despite both having similar signal intensities (Figure 1E), suggesting that the interactions with mitochondria may preferentially involve early/recycling endosomal structures.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential colocalization data between transferrin and EGF endosomes.

claim: Some Tfn-containing endosomes remained in close contact with mitochondria for 3–5 min in live-cell imaging.
source: A number of Tfn-containing endosomes and mitochondria labeled by TagRFP-MTS were observed in close proximity, suggesting possible interactions (Video 1). Some endosomal vesicles remained in close contact with mitochondria for 3–5 min
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Video 1.

claim: Photoirradiation in cells labeled with Mito-Red induces alterations in mitochondrial morphology and the appearance of GFP-Rab5 signals around mitochondria.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that photoirradiation in cells labeled with Mito-Red not only robustly induced alterations in mitochondrial morphology but also the appearance of GFP-Rab5 signals around mitochondria (Figure 2A).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: Mito-Red has been used to perturb mitochondrial function.
source: This is consistent with the fact that certain rosamines and rhodamine-derived dyes used to assay mitochondrial functions possess photosensitizing properties (Hsieh et al., 2015). Specifically, Mito-Red has been used to perturb mitochondrial function (Minamikawa et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Low exposure of Mito-Red labeled cells with a 561 nm laser causes a decrease in mitochondrial and an increase in cytoplasmic signal, indicative of MOMP.
source: Consistent with previous reports, low exposure of Mito-Red labeled cells with a 561 nm laser (~5 J/cm2) caused a decrease in mitochondrial and an increase in cytoplasmic signal, indicative of MOMP
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and is consistent with prior reports, supported by Figure 2A and Video 4.

claim: Laser treatment on Mito-Red-labeled cells results in globular swelling of mitochondria within minutes.
source: Consistent with previous reports, low exposure of Mito-Red labeled cells with a 561 nm laser (~5 J/cm2) caused a decrease in mitochondrial and an increase in cytoplasmic signal, indicative of MOMP, and accompanied by a globular swelling of mitochondria within min (Figure 2A, Video 4).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A and Video 4.

claim: Laser treatment on Mito-Red-labeled cells results in the translocation of GFP-Rab5 to mitochondria.
source: Remarkably, laser treatment on Mito-Red-labeled cells resulted in the translocation of GFP-Rab5 to mitochondria, marked by increased colocalization with Mito-Red compared to the untreated (Figure 2B).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by quantitative colocalization analysis in Figure 2B.

claim: The frequency of GFP-Rab5 early endosomes in close proximity to stressed mitochondria increases after laser treatment.
source: Furthermore, the frequency of GFP-Rab5 EE in close proximity to the stressed mitochondria increased (Figure 2A, Post-laser arrowheads).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: Cells labeled with MitoTracker Green FM retain their tubular mitochondrial structures under laser treatment and do not recruit GFP-Rab5 to the mitochondria.
source: This effect was specific to Mito-Red treatment, because cells labeled with MitoTracker Green FM or transfected with RFP-MTS retained their tubular mitochondrial structures under the same laser treatment and did not recruit GFP-Rab5 to the mitochondria (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cells transfected with RFP-MTS retain their tubular mitochondrial structures under laser treatment and do not recruit GFP-Rab5 to the mitochondria.
source: This effect was specific to Mito-Red treatment, because cells labeled with MitoTracker Green FM or transfected with RFP-MTS retained their tubular mitochondrial structures under the same laser treatment and did not recruit GFP-Rab5 to the mitochondria (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B, respectively).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The recruitment of Rab5 to Mito-Red-labeled mitochondria upon laser-induced stress is visible within 5 min.
source: Time-lapse analysis revealed that the recruitment of Rab5 to rounded mitochondria (Figure 2C, Pre- vs Post-laser) was visible within 5 min
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by time-lapse imaging in Figure 2C-E.

claim: The recruitment of Rab5 to Mito-Red-labeled mitochondria reaches its peak in signal intensity at approximately 15 min post-laser treatment.
source: Time-lapse analysis revealed that the recruitment of Rab5 to rounded mitochondria (Figure 2C, Pre- vs Post-laser) was visible within 5 min and reached its peak in signal intensity at ~15 min post-laser treatment (Figure 2D,E; data correspond to the inset region of Figure 2C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by quantitative analysis in Figure 2D.

claim: The GFP-Rab5 ring-like signal on mitochondria persists for more than 60 min after laser treatment.
source: The GFP-Rab5 ring-like signal persisted for >60 min (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, arrowheads).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Rab5 is recruited to mitochondria in response to signals originating from individually stressed mitochondria.
source: These results suggest that Rab5 is recruited to mitochondria in response to signal(s) originating from individually stressed mitochondria.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localized photoirradiation experiment shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The GFP-Rab5-positive structure observed by CLEM corresponds to a tubular-cisternal structure that is approximately 400 nm in diameter, with the typical morphology of an early endosome.
source: TEM images from three different serial sections of the inset area revealed that the GFP-Rab5-positive structure corresponds to a tubular-cisternal structure that is approximately 400 nm in diameter, with the typical morphology of an early endosome (Figure 3C, green).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by TEM images in Figure 3C.

claim: The endosomal membrane is in very close contact (<5 nm) with the adjacent mitochondrion after laser-induced stress.
source: Serial section analysis showed that the endosomal membrane was in very close contact (<5 nm) with the adjacent mitochondrion of a diameter of ~1.5 µm (Figure 3C, red), which showed few cristae.
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by TEM images in Figure 3C.

claim: The tomogram did not reveal the presence of double or multiple membranes indicative of mitophagy after laser-induced stress.
source: The tomogram showed the presence of membrane contact sites between the rounded mitochondrion and a cisternal structure that could correspond to the ER, but did not reveal the presence of double or multiple membranes indicative of mitophagy (Youle and Narendra, 2011).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by TEM analysis in Figure 3C.

claim: The fast kinetics (minutes) of Rab5 recruitment on rounded mitochondria argues against mitophagy.
source: Following mitochondrial stress, both the fast kinetics (min) of Rab5 recruitment on the rounded mitochondria and the absence of wrapped double-membrane structures argue against mitophagy (Narendra et al., 2008; Novak et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the kinetics data and comparison to known mitophagy timescales.

claim: The absence of wrapped double-membrane structures argues against mitophagy.
source: Following mitochondrial stress, both the fast kinetics (min) of Rab5 recruitment on the rounded mitochondria and the absence of wrapped double-membrane structures argue against mitophagy (Narendra et al., 2008; Novak et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the EM observations and comparison to known mitophagy characteristics.

claim: Mitophagy requires the E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin.
source: Mitophagy requires the E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin (Narendra et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Parkin is normally located in the cytosol but recruited to damaged mitochondria during mitophagy.
source: Mitophagy requires the E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin (Narendra et al., 2008), which is normally located in the cytosol but recruited to damaged mitochondria
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of mitophagy.

claim: Mitophagy involves the formation of LC3-positive autophagosomes and fusion with Lamp1-positive lysosomes in a process that occurs in hours to days.
source: Mitophagy requires the E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin (Narendra et al., 2008), which is normally located in the cytosol but recruited to damaged mitochondria, followed by the formation of LC3-positive autophagosomes and fusion with Lamp1-positive lysosomes in a process that occurs in hours (hr) to days (Dolman et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Cells showed a marginal increase in LC3 and Lamp1 colocalization with Mito-Red in stress-induced cells, with signals mostly concentrated near the perinuclear region.
source: Although we observed a marginal increase in LC3 and Lamp1 colocalization with Mito-Red in stress-induced cells, the signals were mostly concentrated near the perinuclear region (Figure 4B,D,I).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 4B,D,I.

claim: Parkin remained mostly cytoplasmic and did not show enrichment around mitochondria in stress-induced cells.
source: On the other hand, Parkin remained mostly cytoplasmic and did not show enrichment around mitochondria in stress-induced cells (Figure 4F,I).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 4F,I.

claim: The lack of significant Parkin, LC3 and Lamp1 recruitment argues for a mechanism distinct from autophagy and mitophagy.
source: Altogether, the fast kinetics of Rab5 recruitment to stressed mitochondria (<10 min), the absence of a double membranous structure (Figure 3C), and the lack of significant Parkin, LC3 and Lamp1 recruitment argue for a mechanism distinct from autophagy and mitophagy.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: The intrinsic apoptosis pathway is initiated through the activation of the Bax/Bak-mediated MOMP, which leads to the release of cytochrome c to activate effector caspases.
source: The intrinsic pathway is initiated through the activation of the Bax/Bak-mediated MOMP, which leads to the release of cytochrome c to activate effector caspases (Tait and Green, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Upon laser-induced stress, increased Bax puncta around mitochondria were observed compared to untreated cells.
source: Upon laser-induced stress, we observed increased Bax puncta around mitochondria compared to the untreated (Figure 4H,I).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 4H,I.

claim: Cells treated with CCCP exhibit higher Bax fluorescence intensity and colocalization with Mito-Red compared to control cells.
source: Indeed, cells treated with CCCP exhibited higher Bax fluorescence intensity and colocalization with Mito-Red compared to control cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Over-expression of truncated BH3 interacting death domain agonist (tBid) triggers mitochondrial-associated apoptosis.
source: One method of triggering mitochondrial-associated apoptosis is the over-expression of the truncated BH3 interacting death domain agonist (tBid), which is a potent inducer of apoptosis by activating Bax and/or self-oligomerization on mitochondria (Grinberg et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Cells infected with Ad-tBid show a strong enrichment of GFP-Rab5 on mitochondria.
source: We found a strong enrichment of GFP-Rab5 on mitochondria only in cells infected with Ad-tBid but not in Ad-control cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Mitochondrial matrix condensation or swelling is often associated with MOMP by Bax activation, cytochrome c release and subsequent activation of caspases.
source: Morphological changes such as matrix condensation or swelling of mitochondria are often associated with MOMP by Bax activation, cytochrome c release and subsequent activation of caspases (Gottlieb et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: CCCP causes mitochondrial swelling and rounding but without immediate cytochrome c release or cell death.
source: For example, the mitochondrial uncoupler CCCP causes mitochondrial swelling and rounding but without immediate cytochrome c release or cell death (Gao et al., 2001; Lim et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Hydrogen peroxide induces mitochondrial rounding associated with increased Bax expression.
source: On the other hand, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) induces mitochondrial rounding associated with increased Bax expression (Gutiérrez-Venegas et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Hydrogen peroxide induces cytochrome c release and caspase activation.
source: On the other hand, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) induces mitochondrial rounding associated with increased Bax expression (Gutiérrez-Venegas et al., 2015), cytochrome c release and caspase activation (Gutiérrez-Venegas et al., 2015; Takeyama et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Exposure of cells to either CCCP or H2O2 for 2 hr results in mitochondrial rounding and fragmentation.
source: Whereas mitochondria were mostly tubular in control cells (Figure 5A,B, top panels), the exposure of cells to either CCCP or H2O2 for 2 hr resulted in mitochondrial rounding and fragmentation (Figure 5A,B, bottom panels), as previously reported (Narendra et al., 2008; Pletjushkina et al., 2006).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 5A,B.

claim: CCCP did not cause Rab5 enrichment on mitochondria.
source: Interestingly, CCCP did not cause Rab5 enrichment on mitochondria, which was only observed in H2O2-treated cells (Figure 5A,B, arrowheads), quantified as colocalization with Mito-Red (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images and quantification in Figure 5A,C.

claim: H2O2 treatment causes Rab5 enrichment on mitochondria.
source: Interestingly, CCCP did not cause Rab5 enrichment on mitochondria, which was only observed in H2O2-treated cells (Figure 5A,B, arrowheads), quantified as colocalization with Mito-Red (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images and quantification in Figure 5B,D.

claim: The release of cytochrome c into the cytosol is upregulated in H2O2-treated, but not in CCCP-treated cells.
source: Consistent with previous findings, we found that the release of cytochrome c into the cytosol was upregulated in H2O2-treated, but not in CCCP-treated cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis in Figure 5E.

claim: Approximately 62% of cells show strong caspase 3/7 activity in H2O2-treated cells.
source: Using flow cytometry, we detected ~62% of cells showing strong fluorescent signal in H2O2-treated cells
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5F.

claim: Approximately 0.6% of cells show strong caspase 3/7 activity in control cells.
source: Using flow cytometry, we detected ~62% of cells showing strong fluorescent signal in H2O2-treated cells, and merely ~0.6% and~6.2% in control and CCCP-treated cells, respectively.
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5F.

claim: Approximately 6.2% of cells show strong caspase 3/7 activity in CCCP-treated cells.
source: Using flow cytometry, we detected ~62% of cells showing strong fluorescent signal in H2O2-treated cells, and merely ~0.6% and~6.2% in control and CCCP-treated cells, respectively.
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5F.

claim: Only CCCP, but not H2O2, results in the recruitment of GFP-Parkin on mitochondria.
source: As additional controls of the treatment, we showed that only CCCP, but not H2O2, resulted in the recruitment of GFP-Parkin as well as endogenous Parkin on mitochondria (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Injection of CCCP results in a sharp increase in oxygen consumption rate (OCR) compared to media control.
source: Upon the addition of CCCP, a sharp increase in OCR was recorded compared to the media control (Figure 5G, purple vs orange curve).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Seahorse data in Figure 5G.

claim: CCCP causes the collapse of the proton gradient and the disruption of the mitochondrial membrane potential.
source: This is because CCCP causes the collapse of the proton gradient and the disruption of the mitochondrial membrane potential.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of action of CCCP.

claim: Injection of H2O2 results in an initially sharp decline in OCR, but quickly returns to its earlier steady state within 20 min.
source: In contrast, injection of H2O2 resulted in an initially sharp decline in OCR, but quickly returned to its earlier steady state within 20 min (Figure 5G, green curve)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Seahorse data in Figure 5G.

claim: The effect of H2O2 on OCR is reversible.
source: In contrast, injection of H2O2 resulted in an initially sharp decline in OCR, but quickly returned to its earlier steady state within 20 min (Figure 5G, green curve), suggesting that the effect on OCR is reversible.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the OCR data showing recovery.

claim: H2O2 induces the translocation of Rab5 to mitochondria without disrupting the membrane potential.
source: Altogether, our data show that, in addition to activating caspase-dependent apoptotic program, H2O2 also induces the translocation of Rab5 to mitochondria without disrupting the membrane potential.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined observations that H2O2 causes Rab5 translocation but does not cause the same membrane potential collapse as CCCP.

claim: Upon 1 hr H2O2 treatment, there is approximately a 0.5-fold increase in the amount of Rab5 in the cytosolic fraction compared to the control.
source: Consistent with this, upon 1 hr H2O2 treatment, we detected a ~ 0.5-fold increase in the amount of Rab5 in the cytosolic fraction compared to the control (Figure 6A, lane 2,4)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: The cytosolic levels of Rab5 decrease at 2 hr time point after H2O2 treatment.
source: The cytosolic levels of Rab5 then decreased at 2 hr time point (Figure 6A, lane 4,6, Figure 6B).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis and quantification in Figure 6A,B.

claim: There is a marked (~35%) decrease in the colocalization of Rab5 with EEA1 in H2O2-treated compared to untreated cells.
source: We found a marked (~35%) decrease in the colocalization in H2O2-treated compared to untreated cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by colocalization analysis in Figure 6C.

claim: Oxidative stress induces the solubilization of a fraction of Rab5 from the endosomal membrane into the cytosol and its translocation to the mitochondrial membrane.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that oxidative stress induces the solubilization of a fraction of Rab5 from the endosomal membrane into the cytosol and its translocation to the mitochondrial membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the subcellular fractionation and colocalization data.

claim: Cells pre-treated with H2O2 for 10 min show a severe block in transferrin uptake with an accumulation of transferrin signal on the cell surface.
source: In contrast, cells pre-treated with H2O2 for 10 min showed a severe block in Tfn uptake with an accumulation of Tfn signal on the cell surface (Figure 6D,E)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images and quantification in Figure 6D,E.

claim: There is a significant increase in the colocalization between Mito-Red and both Tfn-488 and EGF-488 in H2O2-treated compared to non-treated cells.
source: There was a significant increase in the colocalization between Mito-Red and both Tfn-488 and EGF-488 in H2O2-treated compared to non-treated cells (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images and colocalization analysis in Figure 1C,D.

claim: There is an increase in the total signal intensity of transferrin and EGF in H2O2 conditions.
source: Intriguingly, we also found an increase in the total signal intensity in H2O2 conditions (Figure 1E)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by quantification in Figure 1E.

claim: Transferrin signals accumulate more prominently in the perinuclear region (typical of recycling endosomes) in H2O2 conditions.
source: Intriguingly, we also found an increase in the total signal intensity in H2O2 conditions (Figure 1E), in which Tfn signals accumulated more prominently in the perinuclear region (typical of RE)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1C.

claim: Distinct regions of the mitochondrial network are more prone to rounding and membrane permeabilization than others during H2O2 treatment.
source: By live-cell imaging, we found that mitochondria respond to H2O2 treatment with different kinetics within a cell (Video 8). Distinct regions of the mitochondrial network were more prone to rounding and membrane permeabilization than others, as revealed by the differential loss of Mito-Red during H2O2 treatment (Figure 7A, inset image).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by live-cell imaging in Figure 7A and Video 8.

claim: Regions containing stressed rounded mitochondria correlate exclusively with Rab5 ring-like recruitment.
source: Regions containing stressed rounded mitochondria correlated exclusively with the Rab5 ring-like recruitment (Figure 7A, inset image, arrowheads)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 7A.

claim: There is a significant delay in cytochrome c release from mitochondria in GFP-Rab5 over-expressing cells compared to control cells after H2O2 treatment.
source: We found a significant delay in the cytochrome c release from mitochondria in GFP-Rab5 over-expressing cells compared to control cells (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis and quantification in Figure 7B,C.

claim: Rab5 plays a protective role in mitochondrial-induced apoptosis by down-regulating the release of pro-apoptotic factors to the cytosol.
source: Our results suggest that Rab5 plays a protective role in mitochondrial-induced apoptosis by down-regulating the release of pro-apoptotic factor(s) to the cytosol.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that Rab5 overexpression delays cytochrome c release.

claim: The levels of TOM20 start to increase after 6 hr of H2O2 treatment, suggesting that the mitochondrial mass increases.
source: Interestingly, we found that the levels of TOM20 started to increase after 6 hr, suggesting that the mitochondrial mass increased (Figure 8A, left panels).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis in Figure 8A.

claim: The colocalization between endogenous TOM20 and Rab5 peaks at 6 hr and starts to taper off after 12 hr of H2O2 treatment.
source: In immunostained cells, we found that the colocalization between endogenous TOM20 and Rab5 (Figure 8B) peaked at 6 hr and started to taper off after 12 hr (Figure 8C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 8B,C.

claim: The removal of H2O2 at 12 hr followed by an additional 12 hr incubation in complete medium fully restores the morphology of mitochondria from rounded to tubular.
source: Remarkably, the removal of H2O2 at 12 hr followed by an additional 12 hr incubation in complete medium not only fully restored the morphology of mitochondria from rounded to tubular (Figure 8B, bottom panel)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 8B.

claim: The removal of H2O2 at 12 hr followed by an additional 12 hr incubation in complete medium returns TOM20:Rab5 colocalization to steady state levels.
source: Remarkably, the removal of H2O2 at 12 hr followed by an additional 12 hr incubation in complete medium not only fully restored the morphology of mitochondria from rounded to tubular (Figure 8B, bottom panel), but also returned TOM20:Rab5 colocalization to steady state levels (Figure 8C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by quantification in Figure 8C.

claim: Cells exposed to 500 µM H2O2 show arrested TOM20 levels and are unable to be rescued despite H2O2 removal at 12 hr.
source: The response was dose-dependent as cells exposed to 500 µM H2O2 showed arrested TOM20 levels and were unable to be rescued despite H2O2 removal at 12 hr (Figure 8A, right panels).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis in Figure 8A.

claim: Rab5 translocation to mitochondria induced by oxidative stress is a reversible and protective process responding to apoptotic signals via the regulation of mitochondria.
source: Our data show that Rab5 translocation to mitochondria induced by oxidative stress is a reversible and protective process responding to apoptotic signals via the regulation of mitochondria.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reversibility experiments and the protective effects observed.

claim: Upon laser-induced stress, there is a strong enrichment of Rabenosyn-5, but not EEA1, on mitochondria.
source: Of the tested effectors, we detected a strong enrichment of Rabenosyn-5, but not EEA1, on mitochondria in the same cell (Figure 9A,C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 9A,C.

claim: Neither APPL1 nor APPL2 show enrichment around mitochondria upon laser-induced stress, despite robust Rab5 recruitment.
source: Neither APPL1 nor APPL2 showed enrichment around mitochondria, despite a robust Rab5 recruitment (Figure 9B,C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 9B,C.

claim: GFP-2xFYVEHrs signals remain on vesicle-like puncta and are not present on stressed and swollen mitochondria after 60 min of laser treatment.
source: After 60 min, stressed and swollen mitochondria were observed, but these were completely devoid of GFP signals, which remained on vesicle-like puncta (Figure 9—figure supplements 2, 60 min).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by live-cell imaging in Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claim: Rab5 and Rabenosyn-5, but not EEA1 and APPL1/2, are specifically enriched in the mitochondrial fraction treated with H2O2 compared to non-treated.
source: Consistent with our immunostaining results, Rab5 and Rabenosyn-5, but not EEA1 and APPL1/2, were found to be specifically enriched in the mitochondrial fraction (marked by TOM20) treated with H2O2 compared to non-treated (Figure 9D, lane 2,4).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis in Figure 9D.

claim: The findings reveal a selective mechanism of Rab5 translocation and activation on mitochondria in the absence of PI(3)P.
source: Altogether, our findings reveal a selective mechanism of Rab5 translocation and activation on mitochondria in the absence of PI(3)P.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that PI(3)P probe does not localize to mitochondria while Rab5 and selective effectors do.

claim: Endogenous Rabex-5 remains mostly cytosolic and on cytoplasmic puncta upon laser-induced stress, despite a modest enrichment on mitochondria.
source: Despite a modest enrichment on mitochondria upon laser-induced stress, endogenous Rabex-5 remained mostly cytosolic and on cytoplasmic puncta (Figure 10A)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 10A.

claim: After laser treatment, Alsin exhibits a strong and uniform staining around mitochondria.
source: However, after laser treatment, Alsin exhibited a strong and uniform staining around mitochondria (Figure 10B)
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 10B.

claim: Alsin shows significant colocalization with GFP-Rab5 and Mito-Red after laser treatment.
source: However, after laser treatment, Alsin exhibited a strong and uniform staining around mitochondria (Figure 10B), where it showed significant colocalization with GFP-Rab5 and Mito-Red (Figure 10C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by quantification in Figure 10C.

claim: Over-expression of either Alsin or WT Rab5 prevents caspase 3/7 activation when cells are challenged with H2O2.
source: We tested this idea by over-expressing either Alsin or WT Rab5 in HeLa cells and found that both prevented caspase 3/7 activation as revealed by the weak fluorescence signals (due to the lack of cleavage on the DEVD-conjugated DNA-binding dye) compared to control cells, when challenged with H2O2 (Figure 10—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images and quantification in Figure 10—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Alsin is the gene product of ALS2, which is mutated in multiple neurodegenerative disorders such as juvenile amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), juvenile primary lateral sclerosis (JPLS), and infantile-onset ascending hereditary spastic paralysis (IAHSP).
source: Alsin is the gene product of ALS2, which is mutated in multiple neurodegenerative disorders such as juvenile amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), juvenile primary lateral sclerosis (JPLS), and infantile-onset ascending hereditary spastic paralysis (IAHSP).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Alsin and ALS2.

claim: Alsin comprises three GEF domains: a RCC1-like GEF domain for Ran GTPase, a DH-PH domain for Rho GTPase, and a C-terminal VPS9 domain for Rab5.
source: Alsin comprises three GEF domains: (1) a RCC1-like GEF domain for Ran GTPase, (2) a DH-PH domain for Rho GTPase, and (3) a C-terminal VPS9 domain for Rab5 (Topp et al., 2005) (Figure 10—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature and illustrated in Figure 10—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Functional studies in ALS mouse models have associated Alsin with neuronal survival.
source: Functional studies in ALS mouse models have associated Alsin with neuronal survival (Kanekura et al., 2004; Panzeri et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Functional studies in ALS mouse models have associated Alsin with endolysosomal trafficking.
source: Functional studies in ALS mouse models have associated Alsin with neuronal survival (Kanekura et al., 2004; Panzeri et al., 2006) and endolysosomal trafficking (Hadano et al., 2016; Hadano et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Corticospinal motor neurons in Alsin KO mice display selective defects in mitochondrial morphology.
source: Moreover, corticospinal motor neuron (CSMN) in Alsin KO mice display selective defects in mitochondrial morphology (Gautam et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: At steady state, Alsin localizes to vesicular structures, showing partial overlap with Rab5.
source: At steady state, Alsin localized to vesicular structures, showing partial overlap with Rab5 (Figure 10—figure supplement 1C), consistent with the reported localization of Alsin (Kanekura et al., 2004; Topp et al., 2004).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 10—figure supplement 1C.

claim: WT iPSC-sMNs challenged with H2O2 show a robust enrichment of Rab5 on mitochondria, but not in Alsin-/- iPSC-sMNs.
source: However, WT iPSC-sMNs challenged with H2O2 showed a robust enrichment of Rab5 on mitochondria, but not in Alsin-/- iPSC-sMNs (Figure 11B, H2O2).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence images in Figure 11B.

claim: Cells challenged with H2O2 show a strong enrichment of Rab5 co-fractionating with the mitochondrial fraction in WT iPSC-sMNs, but only weakly in Alsin-/- iPSC-sMNs.
source: On the other hand, cells challenged with H2O2 showed a strong enrichment of Rab5 co-fractionating with the mitochondrial fraction in WT iPSC-sMNs, but only weakly in Alsin-/- iPSC-sMNs (Figure 11C, lane 3,7).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by western blot analysis in Figure 11C.

claim: The lack of Rab5 enrichment in Alsin-/- cells correlates with a greater susceptibility to H2O2-induced apoptotic signaling, as assessed by the rapid release of cytochrome c into the cytosol within 1 hr.
source: The lack of Rab5 enrichment in Alsin-/- cells also correlated with a greater susceptibility to H2O2-induced apoptotic signaling, as assessed by the rapid release of cytochrome c into the cytosol within 1 hr and subsequent accumulation, when compared to WT cells (Figure 11D).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by quantification in Figure 11D.

claim: Alsin is a key regulator for recruiting Rab5 to mitochondria, which imparts a cytoprotective function for cells against oxidative stress.
source: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that Alsin is a key regulator for recruiting Rab5 to mitochondria, which altogether, impart a cytoprotective function for cells against oxidative stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined observations in Alsin-/- cells.

claim: The endocytic system is a primary responder to mitochondria under oxidative stress.
source: Our findings suggest that the endocytic system is a primary responder to mitochondria under oxidative stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Under oxidative stress conditions, the endosomal system appears to rapidly respond to damaged mitochondria through a rescue pathway, which results in the recruitment of Alsin and Rab5 to mitochondria, inhibition of cytochrome c release, decrease in mitochondrial oxygen consumption and hence, increased overall cell viability.
source: Under these conditions, the endosomal system appears to rapidly respond to damaged mitochondria through a rescue pathway, which results in the recruitment of Alsin and Rab5 to mitochondria, inhibition of cytochrome c release, decrease in mitochondrial oxygen consumption and hence, increased overall cell viability (Figure 12).
evidence: This is a summary of the proposed mechanism based on the findings, illustrated in Figure 12.

claim: The mechanism described in this study appears to be distinct from the canonical autophagic/mitophagic mechanisms.
source: Our mechanism appears to be distinct from this as well as the canonical autophagic/mitophagic mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison with known autophagy/mitophagy characteristics.

claim: The recruitment of Rab5 to damaged mitochondria occurs rapidly, within minutes, well preceding any autophagic components analyzed in this study.
source: Third, the recruitment of Rab5 to damaged mitochondria occurs rapidly, that is within min, well preceding any autophagic components that we analyzed in this study.
evidence: This is stated as one of the reasons the mechanism is distinct from autophagy.

claim: Autophagy is restricted to only a subset of small mitochondrial fragments that are LC3+, whereas the majority are devoid of known autophagic markers such as Parkin, LC3 and Lamp1.
source: We found that autophagy is restricted to only a subset of small mitochondrial fragments that are LC3+, whereas the majority are devoid of known autophagic markers such as Parkin, LC3 and Lamp1.
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4.

claim: The data with H2O2 show that the mechanism described here is reversible and argue for a mitochondrial-protective role rather than a degradative process.
source: However, our data with H2O2 show that the mechanism described here is reversible (Figure 8) and argue for a mitochondrial-protective role rather than a degradative process.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the reversibility experiments in Figure 8.

claim: The reversal and recovery of cells from late-stage apoptosis (following cytochrome c release and caspase activation) have been reported in multiple cell lines including HeLa cells and brain cells in a process called 'anastasis'.
source: In fact, the reversal and recovery of cells from late-stage apoptosis (i.e. following cytochrome c release and caspase activation) have recently been reported in multiple cells lines including HeLa cells and brain cells in a process called 'anastasis' (Sun et al., 2017; Tang et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Rabaptin-5 is selectively cleaved by caspase-3 during apoptosis, affecting its interaction with Rab5 and reducing the overall endocytic capacity.
source: For example, Rabaptin-5 is selectively cleaved by caspase-3 during apoptosis, thus affecting its interaction with Rab5 and reducing the overall endocytic capacity (Cosulich et al., 1997; Swanton et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The activation of p38 MAPK by H2O2 stimulates the formation of the GDI:Rab5 complex, favoring the extraction of Rab5 from the early endosomal membrane.
source: The activation of p38 MAPK by H2O2 also stimulates the formation of the GDI:Rab5 complex, thus favoring the extraction of Rab5 from the early endosomal membrane (Cavalli et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: p38 MAPK modulates the endosomal function via phosphorylation and membrane association of Rab5 effectors.
source: In addition, p38 MAPK modulates the endosomal function via phosphorylation and membrane association of Rab5 effectors (Macé et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Hippocampal HT-22 neurons exposed to excess iron exhibit mitochondrial fragmentation and a decrease in cell viability.
source: Interestingly, hippocampal HT-22 neurons exposed to excess iron exhibit mitochondrial fragmentation and a decrease in cell viability (Park et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The C-terminal VPS9 domain of Alsin has GEF activity towards Rab5, and plays a role in Rab5 endosomal localization and dynamics.
source: The C-terminal VPS9 domain of Alsin has GEF activity towards Rab5, and plays a role in Rab5 endosomal localization and dynamics (Otomo et al., 2003; Topp et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The N-terminal RLD of Alsin has been shown to exhibit an autoinhibitory effect on its VPS9 domain.
source: The N-terminal RLD of Alsin has been shown to exhibit an autoinhibitory effect on its VPS9 domain (Otomo et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Mitochondrial-induced stress triggers structural changes in Alsin, releasing the autoinhibitory effect of RLD, thereby exposing the VSP9 domain for Rab5 activation and recruitment.
source: We posit that mitochondrial-induced stress triggers structural changes in the protein, releasing the autoinhibitory effect of RLD, thereby exposing the VSP9 domain for Rab5 activation and recruitment.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the mechanism of Alsin activation.

claim: Alsin was required for Rab5 translocation to mitochondria as this was severely diminished in Alsin-/- iPS-sMN cells.
source: Alsin was required for Rab5 translocation to mitochondria as this was severely diminished in Alsin-/- iPS-sMN cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments in Alsin-/- cells shown in Figure 11.

claim: The presence of (low levels) Rabex-5 on mitochondria detected in HeLa cells suggests that other GEFs may contribute to some Rab5 activation, depending on the cell types, but cannot fully compensate for the loss of Alsin function.
source: The presence of (low levels) Rabex-5 on mitochondria (Figure 10A,C) detected in HeLa cells suggests that other GEFs may contribute to some Rab5 activation, depending on the cell types, but cannot fully compensate for the loss of Alsin function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of modest Rabex-5 enrichment and the severe defect in Alsin-/- cells.

claim: A homologous gene, ALS2CL, containing only the carboxyl-terminal half of ALS2, may also play a role by specifically binding to Rab5 and forming a homodimer with the full-length Alsin to membranous compartments.
source: A homologous gene, ALS2CL, containing only the carboxyl-terminal half of ALS2, may also play a role by specifically binding to Rab5 and forming a homodimer with the full-length Alsin to membranous compartments (Hadano et al., 2004; Suzuki-Utsunomiya et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The Rab5 machinery may be used to bring mitochondria in close proximity to early endosomes and form membrane contact sites.
source: The Rab5 machinery may be used to bring mitochondria in close proximity to EE and form MCS (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the observed increase in MCS.

claim: Membrane contact sites between early endosomes and mitochondria may mediate the transfer of lipids and metabolites.
source: These MCS may mediate the transfer of lipids and metabolites (Helle et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a speculation based on known functions of MCS, supported by citation.

claim: Membrane contact sites between early endosomes and mitochondria may involve 'patching' up mitochondrial wounds by recruiting the ESCRT machinery for closure, or other endomembranes for fusion.
source: These MCS may mediate the transfer of lipids and metabolites (Helle et al., 2013), or involve in 'patching' up mitochondrial wounds by recruiting the ESCRT machinery for closure, or other endomembranes for fusion, both of which are observed in the PM-repair response (Jimenez et al., 2014; Reddy et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a speculation based on known repair mechanisms, supported by citations.

claim: The Rab5 translocation may be a priming step of a stress response pathway that subjects mitochondria to interact with the entire endolysosomal system, in order to modulate the mitochondrial apoptotic potential.
source: Considering that Rab5 is necessary for the biogenesis of the endolysosomal system (Zeigerer et al., 2012), the Rab5 translocation may be a priming step of a stress response pathway that subjects mitochondria to interact with the entire endolysosomal system, in order to modulate the mitochondrial apoptotic potential.
evidence: This is a speculation about the broader implications of Rab5 recruitment.

claim: One quality control mechanism is the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDVs), which are involved in the transport of oxidized or damaged cargo to late endosomes and lysosomes for degradation.
source: One quality control mechanism is the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles (MDVs), which are involved in the transport of oxidized or damaged cargo to LE and lysosomes for degradation (Soubannier et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: MDV formation depends on PINK1/Parkin, but can also occur independently.
source: This process depends on PINK1/Parkin (McLelland et al., 2014), but can also occur independently (Matheoud et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Once recruited onto mitochondria, Rab5 activity may initiate a more extensive endosomal Rab cascade via the Rab coupling/conversion mechanism.
source: Once recruited onto mitochondria, Rab5 activity may not be limited to the recruitment of its effectors, but initiate a more extensive endosomal Rab cascade via the Rab coupling/conversion mechanism.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential downstream effects of Rab5 recruitment.

claim: On early endosomes, Rab5 interacts with divalent effectors, coupling its activity to other Rab proteins (e.g. Rab4, Rab11) that are required for receptor recycling.
source: On EE, Rab5 interacts with divalent effectors, coupling its activity to other Rab proteins (e.g. Rab4, Rab11) that are required for receptor recycling (de Renzis et al., 2002; Vitale et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Rab5 initiates the activation of Rab7, resulting in the conversion of early endosomes into late endosomes.
source: Rab5 also initiates the activation of Rab7, resulting in the conversion of EE into LE (Rink et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: It is possible that the mitochondria-endosome membrane contact sites may evolve over time leading to a Rab7-dependent mitophagic pathway, the engulfment of mitochondria by the early endosomes, or conventional autophagic processes.
source: Therefore, it is possible that the mitochondria-endosome MCS may evolve over time leading to a Rab7-dependent mitophagic pathway (Jimenez-Orgaz et al., 2018), the engulfment of mitochondria by the EE (Hammerling et al., 2017), or conventional autophagic processes (Ao et al., 2014; Stolz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculation about potential long-term outcomes, supported by citations.

claim: Cultured hippocampal neurons from Alsin knockout mice display an accumulation of enlarged Rab5 endosomes and a reduced endosomal motility.
source: Cultured hippocampal neurons from Alsin knockout mice display an accumulation of enlarged Rab5 endosomes and a reduced endosomal motility (Lai et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Mutational and linkage analysis of Alsin from human patients show that the VPS9 domain is critical for Alsin function.
source: Mutational and linkage analysis of Alsin from human patients show that the VPS9 domain is critical for Alsin function (Daud et al., 2016; Verschuuren-Bemelmans et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A recent EM study on the corticospinal motor neurons (CSMN) from Alsin KO mice reveals a selective morphological defect in mitochondria with enlarged core and broken cristae.
source: A recent EM study on the corticospinal motor neurons (CSMN) from Alsin KO mice reveals a selective morphological defect in mitochondria with enlarged core and broken cristae (Gautam et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: WT vs Alsin KO CSMN show no change in Parkin expression, suggesting that mitophagy does not play a major role.
source: Interestingly, WT vs Alsin KO CSMN show no change in Parkin expression, suggesting that mitophagy does not play a major role (Gautam et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The pathological condition of mitochondrial defects in Alsin KO cells is related to a deficiency in Rab5 recruitment to mitochondria, leading to a decline in protection from ROS and oxidative stress associated with aging.
source: We postulate that the pathological condition of mitochondrial defects in Alsin KO cells is related to a deficiency in Rab5 recruitment to mitochondria, thereby leading to a decline in protection from ROS and oxidative stress associated with aging.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the findings of the study.

claim: Mutations in the antioxidant enzyme, superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1), are associated with motor neuron degeneration.
source: Mutations in the antioxidant enzyme, superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1), are associated with motor neuron degeneration.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of ALS research.

claim: In mouse models, an accumulation of the SOD1 mutant proteins results in mitochondrial swelling and increased oxidative damage.
source: In mouse models, an accumulation of the SOD1 mutant proteins results in mitochondrial swelling and increased oxidative damage (Jaarsma et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Loss of Alsin in the mutant SOD1 transgenic mice exacerbates and accelerates disease progression.
source: Interestingly, loss of Alsin in the mutant SOD1 transgenic mice exacerbates and accelerates disease progression (Hadano et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The most common mutation in the multidomain Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) protein in Parkinson disease leads to a hyper-activation of the kinase domain, resulting in hyper-phosphorylation of a number of Rab GTPase substrates including Rab5.
source: In Parkinson disease, the most common mutation in the multidomain Leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) protein leads to a hyper-activation of the kinase domain, resulting in hyper-phosphorylation of a number of Rab GTPase substrates including Rab5 (Steger et al., 2017; Steger et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.
